lines.text: Do you know how a thermos keeps your tea hot for hours? It fights heat in three different ways.
Heat escapes by touch, by moving air, and by glowing out as invisible light.
Between the two walls there's almost nothing. A vacuum. With no air in the gap, heat can't travel by touch or by moving air.
The walls are shiny, like a mirror, so the glowing heat gets bounced back inside.
The weak spot is the top, so a tight stopper seals it. And the same trick keeps cold drinks cold.
It was invented in eighteen ninety two by James Dewar, to keep liquid gases ice cold in his lab.
